  ```
  /usr/bin/ruby -e "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/master/install)"
  ```
  Be sure to add `/usr/local/bin/` to your `$PATH`.

- Install dependencies using Homebrew:
  ```
  brew install autoconf automake libtool bdw-gc boost bison pkg-config
  ```

  Install GMP built in C++11 mode:
  ```
  brew install gmp --c++11
  ```

  By default, Homebrew doesn't link programs into `/usr/local/bin` if
  they would conflict with a version provided by the base system. This
  includes Bison, since an older version ships with macOS. `make
  check` depends on the newer Bison we just installed from Homebrew
  (see [#83](http://github.com/p4lang/p4c/issues/83)), so you'll want
  to add it to your `$PATH` one way or another. One simple way to do
  that is to request that Homebrew link it into `/usr/local/bin`:
  ```
  brew link --force bison
  ```

  Optional documentation building tools:
  ```
  brew install doxygen graphviz
  ```
  Homebrew offers a `protobuf` formula. It installs version 3.2, which should
  work for p4c itself but may cause problems with some extensions. It's
  preferable to install Protocol Buffers 3.0 from source using the instructions
  [here](https://github.com/google/protobuf/blob/master/src/README.md). Check
  out the newest tag in the 3.0 series (`v3.0.2` as of this writing) before you
  build.

## Garbage collector

P4c relies on [BDW garbage collector](https://github.com/ivmai/bdwgc)
to manage its memory.  By default, the p4c exectuables are linked with
the garbage collector library.  In rare cases when the GC causes
problems, this can be disabled by setting `ENABLE_GC` cmake option to
`OFF`.  However, this will dramatically increase the memory usage by the
compiler, and may become impractical for compiling large programs.  **Do
not disable the GC**, unless you really have to.

# Development tools

There is a variety of design and development documentation [here](docs/README.md).

We recommend using `clang++` with no optimizations for speeding up
compilation and simplifying debugging.

We recommend installing a new version of [gdb](http://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gdb).,
because older gdb versions do not always handle C++11 correctly.

We recommend exuberant ctags for navigating source code in Emacs and vi.  `sudo
apt-get install exuberant-ctags.` The Makefile targets `make ctags` and `make
etags` generate tags for vi and Emacs respectively.  (Make sure that you are
using the correct version of ctags; there are several competing programs with
the same name in existence.)

To enable building code documentation, please run `cmake
.. -DENABLE_DOCS=ON`.  This enables the `make docs` rule to generate
documentation. The HTML output is available in
`build/doxygen-out/html/index.html`.

# Docker

A Dockerfile is included. You can generate an image which contains a copy of p4c
in `/p4c/build` by running:

```
docker build -t p4c .
```

On some platforms Docker limits the memory usage of any container, even
containers used during the `docker build` process. On macOS in particular the
default is 2GB, which is not enough to build p4c. Increase the memory limit to
at least 4GB via Docker preferences or you are likely to see "internal compiler
errors" from gcc which are caused by low memory.

# Build system

The build system is based on cmake.  This section describes how it can be customized.

## Defining new CMake targets

When building a new backend target, add it into the development tree in the
extensions subdirectory. The cmake-based build system will automatically include
it if it contains a CMakeLists.txt file.

For a new backend, the cmake file should contain the following rules:

### IR definition files

Backend specific IR definition files should be added to the global list
of IR_DEF_FILES as they are processed together with the core IR files.
Use the following rule:

```
set (IR_DEF_FILES ${IR_DEF_FILES} ${MY_IR_DEF_FILES} PARENT_SCOPE)
```
where `MY_IR_DEF_FILES` is a list of file names with absolute path
(for example, use `${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}`).

If in addition you have additional supporting source files, they
should be added to the frontend sources, as follows:

```
set(EXTENSION_FRONTEND_SOURCES ${EXTENSION_FRONTEND_SOURCES} ${MY_IR_SRCS} PARENT_SCOPE)
```
Again, `MY_IR_SRCS` is a list of file names with absolute path.

### Source files

Sources (.cpp and .h) should be added to the cpplint target using the following rule:

```
add_cpplint_files (${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR} "${MY_SOURCES_AND_HEADERS}")
```

where `mybackend` is the name of the directory you added under extensions.
The p4c CMakeLists.txt will use that name to figure the full path of the files to lint.

### Target

Define a target for your executable. The target should link against
the core `P4C_LIBRARIES` and `P4C_LIB_DEPS`.  `P4C_LIB_DEPS` are
package dependencies. If you need additional libraries for your
project, add them to `P4C_LIB_DEPS`.

In addition, your target should depend on the `genIR` target, since
you need all the IR generation to happen before you start compiling
your backend. If you chose to have your backend as a library (seem the
backends/bmv2 example), the library should depend on `genIR`, and
there is no longer necessary for your executable to depend on it.

```
add_executable(p4c-mybackend ${MY_SOURCES})
target_link_libraries (p4c-mybackend ${P4C_LIBRARIES} ${P4C_LIB_DEPS})
add_dependencies(p4c-mybackend genIR)
```

### Tests

We implemented support equivalent to the automake `make check` rules.
All tests should be included in `make check` and in addition, we support
`make check-*` rules. To enable this support, add the following rules:

```
set(MY_DRIVER <driver or compiler executable>)

set (MY_TEST_SUITES
  ${P4C_SOURCE_DIR}/testdata/p4_16_samples/*.p4
  ${P4C_SOURCE_DIR}/testdata/p4_16_errors/*.p4
  )
set (MY_XFAIL_TESTS
  testdata/p4_16_errors/this_test_fails.p4
 )
p4c_add_tests("mybackend" ${MY_DRIVER} "${MY_TEST_SUITES}" "${MY_XFAIL_TESTS}")
```

In addition, you can add individual tests to a suite using the following macro:
```
set(isXFail FALSE)
set(SWITCH_P4 testdata/p4_14_samples/switch_20160512/switch.p4)

p4c_add_test_with_args ("mybackend" ${MY_DRIVER} ${isXFail}
  "switch_with_custom_profile" ${SWITCH_P4} "-DCUSTOM_PROFILE")
```

See the documentation for
[`p4c_add_test_with_args`](cmake/P4CUtils.cmake) and
[`p4c_add_tests`](cmake/P4CUtils.cmake) for more information on the
arguments to these macros.

To pass custom arguments to p4c, you can set the environment variable `P4C_ARGS`:
```
make check P4C_ARGS="-Xp4c=MY_CUSTOM_FLAG"
```

### Installation

Define rules to install your backend. Typically you need to install
the binary, the additional architecture headers, and the configuration
file for the p4c driver.

```
install (TARGETS p4c-mybackend
  RUNTIME DESTINATION ${P4C_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY})
install (DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/p4include
  DESTINATION ${P4C_ARTIFACTS_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY})
install (FILES ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/driver/p4c.mybackend.cfg
  DESTINATION ${P4C_ARTIFACTS_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY}/p4c_src)
```

# Known issues

The P4C compiler is in early development. Issues with the compiler are
tracked on [GitHub](https://github.com/p4lang/p4c/issues). Before
opening a new issue, please check whether a similar issue is already
opened. Opening issues and submitting a pull request with fixes for
those issues is much appreciated.

In addition to the list of issues on Github, there are a number of
currently unsupported features listed below:

## Frontend

### P4_14 features not supported in P4_16

* extern/blackbox attributes -- there is support for carrying them in
the IR, but they are lost if P4_16 code is output.  Backends can
access them from the IR

* Nonstandard extension primitives from P4_14
  * Execute_meter extra arguments
  * Recirculate variants
  * Bypass_egress
  * Sample_ primitives
  * invalidate

* No support for P4_14 parser exceptions.

## Backends

### Bmv2 Backend

* Range "set" not supported in parser transitions
* Tables with multiple apply calls

See also [unsupported P4_16 language features](backends/bmv2/README.md#unsupported-p4_16-language-features).
annotation: Implement a basic packet parser and forwarding pipeline with ingress and egress processing
detailed_annotation: Uses a parser to extract packet data into a custom header format (`my_packet`) based on a simple header definition (`data_h`).
Employs a value set (`value_set_t`) with an inner structure (`inner_value_set_t`) for lookups during packet parsing.
Ingress processing applies a table (`t`) that matches on metadata (`meta.data[0].da`) and supports a single action (`set_data`).
The pipeline includes empty, but defined, control blocks for verifying checksums (`MyVerifyChecksum`), computing checksums (`MyComputeChecksum`), and deparsing packets (`MyDeparser`).

desc: This repository contains an updated p4c compiler and a corresponding BMv2 software switch, which can handle Double precision numbers
raw_readme:
[![Build Status](https://travis-ci.org/p4lang/p4c.svg?branch=master)](https://travis-ci.org/p4lang/p4c)

# p4c

p4c is a new, alpha-quality reference compiler for the P4 programming language.
It supports both P4-14 and P4-16; you can find more information about P4
[here](http://p4.org) and the specifications for both versions of the language
[here](https://p4.org/specs).

p4c is modular; it provides a standard frontend and midend which can be combined
with a target-specific backend to create a complete P4 compiler. The goal is to
make adding new backends easy.

The code contains four sample backends:
* p4c-bm2-ss: can be used to target the P4 `simple_switch` written using
  the BMv2 behavioral model https://github.com/p4lang/behavioral-model
* p4c-ebpf: can be used to generate C code which can be compiled to EBPF
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley_Packet_Filter and then loaded
  in the Linux kernel for packet filtering
* p4test: a source-to-source P4 translator which can be used for
  testing, learning compiler internals and debugging.
* p4c-graphs: can be used to generate visual representations of a P4 program;
  for now it only supports generating graphs of top-level control flows.

Sample command lines:

Compile P4_16 or P4_14 source code.  If your program successfully
compiles, the command will create files with the same base name as the
P4 program you supplied, and the following suffixes instead of the
`.p4`:

+ a file with suffix `.p4i`, which is the output from running the
  preprocessor on your P4 program.
+ a file with suffix `.p4rt`, which is a binary format containing a
  description of the tables and other objects in your P4 program that
  have an auto-generated control plane API.
+ a file with suffix `.json` that is the JSON file format expected by
  BMv2 behavioral model `simple_switch`.

```bash
p4c --target bmv2 --arch v1model my-p4-16-prog.p4
p4c --target bmv2 --arch v1model --std p4-14 my-p4-14-prog.p4
```

All of these commands take the `--help` argument to show documentation
of supported command line options.  `p4c --target-help` shows the
supported "target, arch" pairs.

```bash
p4c --help
p4c --target-help
```

Auto-translate P4_14 source to P4_16 source:

```bash
p4test --std p4-14 my-p4-14-prog.p4 --pp auto-translated-p4-16-prog.p4
```

Check syntax of P4_16 or P4_14 source code, without limitations that
might be imposed by any particular compiler back end.  There is no
output for these commands other than error and/or warning messages.

```bash
p4test my-p4-16-prog.p4
p4test --std p4-14 my-p4-14-prog.p4
```

Generate GraphViz ".dot" files for parsers and controls of a P4_16 or
P4_14 source program.

```bash
p4c-graphs my-p4-16-prog.p4
p4c-graphs --std p4-14 my-p4-14-prog.p4
```

Generate PDF of parser instance named "ParserImpl" generated by the
`p4c-graphs` command above (search for graphviz below for its install
instructions):

```bash
dot -Tpdf ParserImpl.dot > ParserImpl.pdf
```

# Getting started

1.  Clone the repository. It includes submodules, so be sure to use
    `--recursive` to pull them in:
    ```
    git clone --recursive https://github.com/p4lang/p4c.git
    ```
    If you forgot `--recursive`, you can update the submodules at any time using:
    ```
    git submodule update --init --recursive
    ```

2.  Install [dependencies](#dependencies). You can find specific instructions
    for Ubuntu 16.04 [here](#ubuntu-dependencies) and for macOS 10.12
    [here](#macos-dependencies).

3.  Build. Building should also take place in a subdirectory named `build`.
    ```
    mkdir build
    cd build
    cmake .. <optional arguments>
    make -j4
    make -j4 check
    ```
    The cmake command takes the following optional arguments to
    further customize the build:
     - `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RELEASE|DEBUG` -- set CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE to
      RELEASE or DEBUG to build with optimizations or with debug
      symbols to run in gdb. Default is RELEASE.
     - `-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=<path>` -- set the directory where
       `make install` installs the compiler. Defaults to /usr/local.
     - `-DENABLE_BMV2=ON|OFF`. Enable the bmv2 backend. Default ON.
     - `-DENABLE_EBPF=ON|OFF`. Enable the ebpf backend. Default ON.
     - `-DENABLE_P4C_GRAPHS=ON|OFF`. Enable the p4c-graphs backend. Default ON.
     - `-DENABLE_P4TEST=ON|OFF`. Enable the p4test backend. Default ON.
     - `-DENABLE_DOCS=ON|OFF`. Build documentation. Default is OFF.
     - `-DENABLE_GC=ON|OFF`. Enable the use of the garbage collection
       library. Default is ON.
     - `-DENABLE_GTESTS=ON|OFF`. Enable building and running GTest unit tests.
       Default is ON.
     - `-DENABLE_PROTOBUF_STATIC=ON|OFF`. Enable the use of static
       protobuf libraries. Default is ON.

    If adding new targets to this build system, please see
    [instructions](#defining-new-cmake-targets).

4.  (Optional) Install the compiler and the P4 shared headers globally.
    ```
    sudo make install
    ```
    The compiler driver `p4c` and binaries for each of the backends are
    installed in `/usr/local/bin` by default; the P4 headers are placed in
    `/usr/local/share/p4c`.

5.  You're ready to go! You should be able to compile a P4-16 program for BMV2
    using:
    ```
    p4c -b bmv2-ss-p4org program.p4 -o program.bmv2.json
    ```

If you plan to contribute to p4c, you'll find more useful information
[here](#development-tools).

# Dependencies

Ubuntu 16.04 is the officially supported platform for p4c. There's also
unofficial support for macOS 10.12. Other platforms are untested; you can try to
use them, but YMMV.

- A C++11 compiler. GCC 4.9 or later or Clang 3.3 or later is required.

- `git` for version control

- GNU autotools for the build process

- CMake 3.0.2 or higher

- Boehm-Weiser garbage-collector C++ library

- GNU Bison and Flex for the parser and lexical analyzer generators.

- Google Protocol Buffers 3.0 or higher for control plane API generation

- GNU multiple precision library GMP

- C++ boost library (minimally used)

- Python 2.7 for scripting and running tests

- Optional: Documentation generation (enabled when configuring with
  --enable-doxygen-doc) requires Doxygen (1.8.10 or higher) and Graphviz
  (2.38.0 or higher).

Backends may have additional dependencies. The dependencies for the backends
included with `p4c` are documented here:
  * [BMv2](backends/bmv2/README.md)
  * [eBPF](backends/ebpf/README.md)
  * [graphs](backends/graphs/README.md)

Most dependencies can be installed using `apt-get install`:

libfl-dev libgmp-dev libboost-dev libboost-iostreams-dev
libboost-graph-dev llvm pkg-config python python-scapy python-ipaddr python-ply
tcpdump`

annotation: Implement a basic packet parser and processor pipeline.
detailed_annotation: Parses incoming packets into a custom `my_packet` structure using a stateful parser `MyParser`.
Tracks metadata across pipeline stages using `my_metadata`, which stores an array of `data_h` structures.

Includes a deparser `MyDeparser` that processes the packet for output, although its apply block is empty.
Features a checksum verification control `MyVerifyChecksum`, albeit with an empty apply block, indicating a potential placeholder for future implementation.

[![Build Status](https://travis-ci.org/cornell-netlab/petr4.svg?branch=use-poulet4)](https://travis-ci.org/cornell-netlab/petr4)

# Petr4
The Petr4 project is developing the formal semantics of the [P4
Language](https://p4.org) backed by an independent reference implementation.

# POPL'21 artifact
See https://verified-network-toolchain.github.io/petr4/ or check out the `gh-pages` branch
for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).
annotation: Implement a basic packet processing pipeline with ingress and egress controls.
detailed_annotation: Ingress control marks packets to be dropped using the `mark_to_drop` function.
Egress control does not modify packet headers or metadata.
Parser and deparser are present but do not perform any operations.
No checksum computation or packet transformation is performed.
The pipeline uses a simple state machine in the parser with a single transition to accept.

annotation: Implement a packet forwarding pipeline with ingress routing based on header field matching
detailed_annotation: Ingress pipeline uses a table `t_exact` to match on the `e` field of the `row_t` header structure with exact matching.
The table `t_exact` has two actions: `a` and `a_with_control_params`, where `a` sets the egress spec to 0 and `a_with_control_params` sets it to a specified value.
The ingress pipeline applies the `t_exact` table and performs actions based on the match results.
The parser extracts the header from the packet and the deparser emits the header back to the packet.
The pipeline includes empty control blocks for verification (`vrfy`), update, and egress processing.

annotation: Implement header parsing and transformation based on header type
detailed_annotation: Uses a parser to extract headers from incoming packets, with conditional transitions based on header values.
Employs a header union to represent alternative header formats (Hdr1 and Hdr2).
Performs packet transformation in the ingress control by invalidating Hdr2 if it is valid.
Emits extracted headers in the deparser, ensuring correct packet output.
Utilizes a state machine in the parser to manage different header extraction states (start, getH1, getH2).

annotation: Implement IPv4 checksum verification and packet processing
detailed_annotation: Verify IPv4 header checksum using `verify_checksum` function in the `vc` control
Parse Ethernet, IPv4, and TCP headers in the `parserI` parser
Modify the IPv4 header's TTL field without updating the checksum field in the `cIngress` control
Handle parser errors and checksum errors by modifying output packet headers in the `cIngress` control
Use a custom `V1Switch` architecture with multiple controls (`vc`, `cIngress`, `cEgress`, `uc`, and `DeparserI`)

annotation: Implement a parser and packet processor that extracts and transforms Ethernet and custom headers.
detailed_annotation: Protocol-specific parsing: The parser uses EtherType values to determine which custom header to extract (h0, h1, h2, h3, or h4).
State tracking: The parser uses a state machine to extract headers based on EtherType values.
Packet transformation: The ingress control overwrites specific bits of the Ethernet destination address based on the validity of custom headers.
Header validity checking: The ingress control checks the validity of custom headers (h0, h1, h2, h3, h4) to determine which bits to overwrite in the Ethernet destination address.

[![Build Status](https://travis-ci.org/cornell-netlab/petr4.svg?branch=use-poulet4)](https://travis-ci.org/cornell-netlab/petr4)

# Petr4
The Petr4 project is developing the formal semantics of the [P4
Language](https://p4.org) backed by an independent reference implementation.

# POPL'21 artifact
See https://verified-network-toolchain.github.io/petr4/ or check out the `gh-pages` branch
for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).
annotation: Implement conditional header parsing and modification based on Ethernet source address and EtherType.
detailed_annotation: Conditional parsing: The parser uses a select expression to determine which header to parse next based on the Ethernet source address and EtherType.
Header modification: The ingress control overwrites specific bits of the Ethernet destination address based on the validity of parsed headers.
Parser state machine: The parser uses a state machine with multiple states (start, parse_h0, parse_h1, etc.) to extract headers conditionally.
Header validity tracking: The program tracks the validity of parsed headers (e.g., hdr.h0.isValid()) to make decisions in the ingress control.
Egress specification: The ingress control sets the egress_spec metadata field to a fixed value (3).

annotation: Implement a basic IPv4 router with MAC rewriting and checksum verification
detailed_annotation: Parses Ethernet and IPv4 headers using a stateful parser with multiple states (parse_ethernet, parse_ipv4, etc.)
Performs longest prefix matching (LPM) and exact matching for IPv4 FIB lookups in the ingress control
Rewrites source and destination MAC addresses in the egress control using a table-based approach
Verifies and computes IPv4 header checksums using a checksum algorithm (HashAlgorithm.csum16) in separate control blocks
Uses metadata to track ingress information, such as VRF, BD, and nexthop index, for routing decisions

annotation: Implement IPv4 header checksum verification and computation.
detailed_annotation: Conditional checksum computation: The program uses a conditional statement to invoke the checksum computation only when the IPv4 header length (ihl) is 5.
Checksum verification: The program includes a VerifyChecksumI control that presumably checks the integrity of the IPv4 header checksum.
Checksum computation: The program uses the update_checksum function with HashAlgorithm.csum16 to compute the IPv4 header checksum.
IPv4 header parsing: The program defines a parser (ParserI) and a header structure (H) to process IPv4 packets.
Standard metadata processing: The program includes standard metadata processing in the IngressI, EgressI, and DeparserI controls.

annotation: Implement a basic Ethernet packet parser and processor pipeline
detailed_annotation: Parses Ethernet headers using a stateful parser with two states: `start` and `parse_ethernet`.
Uses a compound action `my_drop` to mark packets for drop, as required by the P4_16 compiler.
Defines a pipeline with separate controls for ingress, egress, and deparser, each with an empty apply block.
Includes placeholder controls for verifying and computing checksums, which currently have empty apply blocks.
Uses the V1Switch architecture to compose the parser, ingress, egress, and deparser controls into a single pipeline.

annotation: Implement a basic network packet processing pipeline with parsing, verification, and transformation.
detailed_annotation: Uses a custom parser `MyParser` to extract a header stack with 100 elements from incoming packets.
Employs a set of control blocks (`MyIngress`, `MyEgress`, `MyComputeChecksum`) with empty apply blocks, indicating no modifications to packets.
Includes a deparser `MyDeparser` that emits the header stack back into the packet.
Features a checksum verification control block `MyVerifyChecksum`, although its apply block is empty, suggesting no actual verification is performed.
Organizes the pipeline using the `V1Switch` architecture, integrating the custom parser, control blocks, and deparser.

Verify the checksum of IPv4 headers using a 16-bit checksum algorithm
Filter packets based on IPv4 source addresses using a ternary match
Update the egress specification based on the result of the LPM table lookup
Drop packets with invalid IPv4 headers or that do not match the LPM table

# Petr4
The Petr4 project is developing the formal semantics of the [P4
Language](https://p4.org) backed by an independent reference implementation.

# POPL'21 artifact
See https://verified-network-toolchain.github.io/petr4/ or check out the `gh-pages` branch
for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).
annotation: Implement a basic packet forwarding pipeline with a debug table.
detailed_annotation: Uses a debug table to drop or forward packets based on a metadata field `test`.
Tracks a boolean metadata field `test` across pipeline stages.
Utilizes a register to store and retrieve a single-bit value.
Applies actions based on the metadata field `test` using a table with exact matching.
Drops or forwards packets using standard actions.

annotation: Implement a basic network switch with ingress processing and static action application
detailed_annotation: Uses a single table `test_table` with an exact match key on `meta.test` to select an action `act` with a parameter of type `test_t`.
Applies a static action `act` with parameter `1` to packets that match the `test_table` entry.
Tracks metadata in the `metadata` struct, specifically a byte field `test`.
Employs a simple parser with no header parsing logic, immediately transitioning to an accept state.
Defines several empty control blocks (`VerifyChecksumImpl`, `EgressImpl`, `ComputeChecksumImpl`, `DeparserImpl`) likely intended for future extension or boilerplate implementation.

annotation: Implement a custom protocol parser and packet processor
detailed_annotation: Parses custom protocol headers, including `prot_common_t`, `prot_addr_common_t`, and `prot_host_addr_t`, with conditional parsing based on header types.
Tracks metadata, such as `currenti_t` and `headerLen`, to guide parsing and processing decisions.

annotation: Implement a protocol-aware address parser and packet processor
detailed_annotation: Uses a header union `addr_t` with type-specific fields for IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
Employs a parser `ProtAddrParser` that extracts address information based on a given address type.

Features a modular architecture with separate controls for ingress, egress, and checksum computation processing.

annotation: Implement Ethernet packet processing with metadata manipulation
detailed_annotation: Parses Ethernet headers from incoming packets using a custom parser `parserImpl`.
Manipulates metadata structures (`mystruct1_t` and `mystruct2_t`) within the `ingressImpl` control.
Assigns values to metadata fields using struct literal syntax (e.g., `meta.s2 = {s1=meta.s1, f3=5, f4=8};`).
Transforms metadata values into egress specification using bit casting (e.g., `stdmeta.egress_spec = (bit<9>) meta.s2.s1.f2;`).
Emits Ethernet headers from outgoing packets using a custom deparser `deparserImpl`.

annotation: Implement conditional parsing and header transformation based on packet type
detailed_annotation: Conditional parsing: The parser uses a `select` statement to choose between parsing `O1` or `O2` headers based on the value of `hdr.base.t`.
Header union handling: The program uses a header union `U` with two possible headers `O1` and `O2`, and applies different parsing and transformation logic based on which header is valid.
Packet transformation: The ingress control modifies the packet headers based on the validity of the `O1` and `O2` headers, setting valid flags and modifying data fields.
Table-based processing: The ingress control uses a table `debug_hdr` to perform lookups based on header fields, although in this case, it only applies the `NoAction`.

annotation: Implement runtime-indexed header vector access and modification
detailed_annotation: Uses runtime indices to access and modify elements of a header vector (`vec_e_t`) within the `ingress` control.
Supports arithmetic expressions as indices, including those involving other header fields and bitwise operations.

annotation: Implement a parser and packet processor for custom Ethernet packets with variable-length headers.
detailed_annotation: Parses custom Ethernet packets with variable-length headers using a stateful parser (`parserImpl`).
Tracks parser errors and encodes them into the packet's Ethernet destination address (`ingressImpl`).

annotation: Implement a parser and pipeline for custom Ethernet packets with variable-length headers
detailed_annotation: Parses custom Ethernet packets with variable-length headers using a stateful parser (`parserImpl`) that extracts headers based on EtherType.
Tracks parser errors and maps them to a numerical value, which is then written to the `dstAddr` field of the Ethernet header (`ingressImpl`).
Emits the parsed Ethernet header back to the packet in the deparser stage (`deparserImpl`).
Includes a verify checksum control, but it does not perform any actual checksum verification (`verifyChecksum`).
The pipeline consists of ingress, egress, and update checksum controls, but they do not perform any significant actions.

annotation: Implement a parser that sets egress spec metadata in a specific sequence
detailed_annotation: The parser, MyParser, transitions through multiple states to set the egress_spec metadata in a specific sequence: 1, 2, 3, 4, then 5.
The parser uses a state machine with select statements to determine the next state based on input values.
The egress_spec metadata is updated at each state, with the final state being fifth_state with a value of 5.
The parser uses a combination of fixed and wildcard values to determine the next state.
The program uses P4's V1Switch architecture, comprising multiple control blocks (MyChecksum, MyIngress, MyEgress, MyDeparser) in addition to the parser.

annotation: Implement a parser with subparser inlining for header processing
detailed_annotation: Uses a subparser (`Subparser`) instance with two invocations and same arguments, but different transitions after invocations.
Employs state tracking with multiple states (`start`, `p0`, `p1`, `p2`, `p3`, `p4`) and transitions based on `standard_metadata.ingress_port`.
Performs packet transformations by extracting headers (`h1`, `h2`, `h3`) and modifying header fields (`hdr.f = 42`).
Applies conditional logic to set `standard_metadata.egress_spec` based on header field values (`hdr.h1.f == 42`).
Utilizes a deparser (`DeparserImpl`) to emit headers (`h1`, `h2`) to the packet output.

annotation: Implement packet parsing with conditional header extraction and metadata processing
detailed_annotation: Uses a subparser (`Subparser`) with multiple states and conditional transitions to extract headers based on packet data.
The subparser is instantiated and applied twice in the main parser (`ParserImpl`) with different ingress ports.
Header validity checks are performed in the ingress control to determine egress specifications.
Packet headers are emitted in the deparser based on the ingress processing results.
Conditional extraction of headers (`h3`, `h4`) is based on state transitions in the subparser and main parser.

# Petr4
The Petr4 project is developing the formal semantics of the [P4
Language](https://p4.org) backed by an independent reference implementation.

# POPL'21 artifact
See https://verified-network-toolchain.github.io/petr4/ or check out the `gh-pages` branch
for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).
annotation: Implement a parser that extracts headers and applies subparser logic based on ingress port.
detailed_annotation: Uses a subparser (`Subparser`) instance with two invocations and different arguments in the main parser (`ParserImpl`).
Applies state transition based on ingress port to decide which header to process with the subparser.
Extracts headers (`h1` and `h2`) from the packet in the main parser.
Modifies the `egress_spec` in the `standard_metadata` based on the value of a header field (`hdr.h1.f`).
Emits headers back to the packet in the deparser (`DeparserImpl`).

[![Build Status](https://travis-ci.org/cornell-netlab/petr4.svg?branch=use-poulet4)](https://travis-ci.org/cornell-netlab/petr4)

# Petr4
The Petr4 project is developing the formal semantics of the [P4
Language](https://p4.org) backed by an independent reference implementation.

# POPL'21 artifact
See https://verified-network-toolchain.github.io/petr4/ or check out the `gh-pages` branch
for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).
annotation: Implement Ethernet packet processing with logging and data type demonstrations
detailed_annotation: Demonstrates various data type operations, including boolean, bit, signed and unsigned integer, enum, and serializable enum types.
Parses Ethernet packets and extracts headers.
Logs values of different data types using the `log_msg` function.
Handles enum and serializable enum types with conditional assignments based on packet header values.
Emits Ethernet packets in the deparser.

annotation: Implement a P4 switch that extracts and matches on port IDs
detailed_annotation: Extracts port IDs from packet headers using a parser.
Matches on exact values of three different port ID types (PortId1_t, PortId2_t, PortId3_t) in an ingress table.
Supports multiple port ID types with different representations (uint, bit, string) using P4Runtime translations.
Emits extracted headers back to the packet in the deparser.
Includes a verification control with an empty apply block.

annotation: Implement a basic Ethernet packet processor with ingress logic
detailed_annotation: Parses Ethernet headers from incoming packets using a stateful parser.
Modifies Ethernet header fields (source and destination addresses, EtherType) in the ingress control.
Applies a simple action in ingress that conditionally skips processing based on the EtherType.
Uses a sequence of actions (`dummy` and `dummy2`) to update header fields in a specific order.
Emits parsed headers back to the packet output in the deparser control.

annotation: Implement conditional header extraction based on lookahead values
detailed_annotation: Uses a parser to conditionally extract headers based on the values of `f1` in the first three headers.
Tracks the number of headers extracted and stores it in the `h_count` field of the `meta` struct.
Supports four different extraction paths based on the values of `f1` in the headers.
Utilizes a state machine with five states (`start`, `one`, `two`, `three`, and `many`) to manage the extraction process.
Transitions between states are determined by the values of `f1` in the headers.

annotation: Implement a P4 switch that extracts and transforms headers based on runtime indexes and metadata.
detailed_annotation: Uses runtime indexes to access and modify packet headers, specifically with `hdr.pool[i].val` and `hdr.vector[1].e`.
Tracks metadata, including a counter that increments on each packet processed in the ingress stage.
Extracts and processes multiple headers, including Ethernet, custom `ml_hdr_t`, and arrays of `vec_e_t` and `aggregator_t`.
Modifies packet headers based on arithmetic operations, such as adding 1 to `hdr.pool[1].val` and `hdr.pool[i].base1`.
Emits modified packet headers back out through the deparser.

Language](https://p4.org) backed by an independent reference implementation.

# POPL'21 artifact
See https://verified-network-toolchain.github.io/petr4/ or check out the `gh-pages` branch
for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).
annotation: Implement Ethernet packet parser and logger
detailed_annotation: Parses Ethernet packets and extracts destination and source addresses, and etherType.
Validates the Ethernet header using the `isValid()` method and logs the result.
Demonstrates the use of `isValid()` on various header types, including a header, a header union, and a header stack.
Emits the parsed Ethernet header back out to the packet in the deparser.
Logs messages at ingress based on validity of headers and header components.

annotation: Implement packet processing with header parsing, modification, and cloning
detailed_annotation: Parses packet headers into `bitvec_hdr` structures (`bvh0` and `bvh1`) using the `parse` function.
Modifies header fields in the `ingress` control, including setting `valid` bits and updating `port` values.
Clones packets using the `clone_preserving_field_list` function with `CloneType.I2E`.
Emits modified headers in the `deparser` control.
Tracks and updates local metadata, including `row_t` and `col_t` structures.

annotation: Implement a basic P4 switch with ingress, egress, and deparser functionality
detailed_annotation: Ingress port modification: The parser sets the ingress port to 2 if it is initially 0.
Empty control blocks: The ingress, egress, verify checksum, compute checksum, and deparser controls have empty apply blocks.
Standard metadata handling: The switch uses standard metadata, including ingress port.
No packet transformation: The deparser and controls do not modify packet headers.
No checksum computation: The verify checksum and compute checksum controls have no implementation.

annotation: Implement Ethernet header validation and modification
detailed_annotation: Parses Ethernet headers from incoming packets using a custom parser `MyParser`.
Validates Ethernet headers using the `isValid()` method and performs a series of bitwise operations on the `f` field in the `MyIngress` control.
Emits modified Ethernet headers back to packets in the `MyDeparser` control.
Uses a custom series of actions `do_round` and `do_n_rounds` to perform repeated bitwise operations on the `f` field.
Integrates with the V1Switch architecture, incorporating ingress, egress, and deparser controls.

for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).
annotation: Implement a parser and pipeline for custom variable-length header processing
detailed_annotation: Parses custom variable-length headers with a dynamic number of varbits based on the `n_varbits` field in the `error_code_t` header.
Tracks parser errors and maps them to a specific error code in the `error_code_t` header.
Emits the parsed headers without modification in the deparser.
Supports a custom header structure with a variable-length field (`custom_var_len_t`).
Does not perform any checksum verification or updates.

annotation: Implement a simple packet processor that extracts and transforms header data
detailed_annotation: Extracts an array of 10 bytes from incoming packets using a parser.
Modifies specific bytes in the extracted header array using a function that assigns fixed values (0xAA and 0xBB).
Applies a transformation to specific bytes in the header array based on argument order.
Emits the transformed header array back to the packet.
Utilizes a deparser to reconstruct the packet with the modified header.

annotation: Implement a P4 switch that modifies packet headers by swapping and modifying byte values.
detailed_annotation: The parser `MyParser` extracts 6 bytes from the packet into an array `arr` in the `hdr_t` header.
The ingress control `MyIngress` modifies the extracted byte array by swapping and modifying pairs of bytes using the function `f`.
The function `f` takes two bytes as input, and sets their values to 0xAA and 0xBB, respectively.
The deparser `MyDeparser` emits the modified byte array back into the packet.
The ingress and egress controls do not perform any checksum computation or packet filtering, but only modify the packet headers.
